landmarks.name: Eiffel Tower
landmarks.writeup: An iconic iron lattice tower in Paris, symbolizing French art and engineering.

wiki.extract: The Eiffel Tower is a lattice tower on the Champ de Mars in Paris, France. It is named after the engineer Gustave Eiffel, whose company designed and built the tower from 1887 to 1889.

landmarks.name: Louvre Museum
landmarks.writeup: World's largest art museum, home to the Mona Lisa and vast historical collections.

wiki.extract: The Louvre is a national art museum in Paris, France. It is located on the Right Bank of the Seine in the city's 1st arrondissement (district) and home to some of the most canonical works of Western art, including the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and Winged Victory. The museum is housed in the Louvre Palace, originally built in the late 12th to 13th century under Philip II. Remnants of the Medieval Louvre fortress are visible in the basement of the museum. Due to urban expansion, the fortress eventually lost its defensive function, and in 1546 Francis I converted it into the primary residence of the French kings.

landmarks.name: Mont Saint-Michel
landmarks.writeup: A medieval abbey perched on a rocky island, known for its unique tides and architecture.

wiki.extract: Mont-Saint-Michel is a tidal island and mainland commune in Normandy, France.

landmarks.name: Palace of Versailles
landmarks.writeup: A former royal residence famous for its opulent architecture and gardens.

wiki.extract: The Palace of Versailles is a château and historic monument in Versailles in the Yvelines department of France, southwest of Paris. It served as the principal residence of the French kings Louis XIV, Louis XV, and Louis XVI.

landmarks.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: A masterpiece of Gothic architecture located in Paris, renowned for its stained glass and sculptures.

wiki.extract: On 15 April 2019, at 18:18 CEST, a structural fire broke out in the roof space of Notre-Dame de Paris, a medieval Catholic cathedral in Paris, France, part of the "Paris, Banks of the Seine" UNESCO World Heritage Site.

cultural_events.name: Bastille Day
cultural_events.writeup: National day on July 14th commemorating the French Revolution with parades and fireworks.

cultural_events.name: Cannes Film Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An internationally acclaimed film festival showcasing new films from around the world.

cultural_events.name: Tour de France
cultural_events.writeup: The world's most famous cycling race held annually across various regions of France.

cultural_events.name: Nice Carnival
cultural_events.writeup: A vibrant winter festival featuring parades, floats, and street performances.

cultural_events.name: Fête de la Musique
cultural_events.writeup: A nationwide music celebration held on June 21st promoting live music in public spaces.

food_writeup: French cuisine is renowned for its diversity and quality, featuring dishes like baguettes, cheese, wine, croissants, coq au vin, and ratatouille. It emphasizes fresh ingredients, regional specialties, and culinary techniques that have influenced global gastronomy.
brief_history: France has a rich history from ancient Gaul through the Roman era, the medieval kingdom, the Renaissance, and the French Revolution which shaped modern democracy. It played key roles in both World Wars and is a founding member of the European Union.

important_people.name: Charles de Gaulle
important_people.description: Leader of Free France and president

current_conflicts: France is not engaged in any active military conflicts but participates in international peacekeeping and counter-terrorism operations.
